summary: A change to Medicaid has a different local story depending on the affected industry.
realLife: A study of Louisiana hospitals found that unpaid care took up a smaller share of operating costs after Medicaid expanded. The decline was larger at rural hospitals than at urban ones.
inGame: needs: a played industry outcome traceable to the Medicaid change; the expansion-match law and law-industry comparison exist.
gates: The coverage change has a supported local industry effect.

turns.what: A clinic changes its hours when the first post-change payments arrive.
turns.pulledBy: Its operating decision depends on actual reimbursements after the coverage change.
turns.writesBack: The new schedule starts in the payment period that prompted it.

turns.what: At the hospital board meeting, the treasurer reports fewer bills going unpaid and asks to leave the clinic hours alone for now.
turns.pulledBy: The quarterly report shows the change in uncompensated care, and the staffing appropriation has yet to come up for a vote.
turns.writesBack: The board records the financial result and keeps the existing hours on the patient calendar.
